newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-TABLE-TOPPING UNITED SEEK REVENGE OVER SAINTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TABLE-TOPPING UNITED SEEK REVENGE OVER SAINTS.

text.p: New leaders Manchester United seek revenge against Southampton in the English premier league on Saturday while London rivals Chelsea and Tottenham lock horns in the capital's top match.
United, playing their most attractive football of the season, beat Wimbledon to go top of the table on Wednesday and have now taken 28 points out of a possible 36 in their last 12 matches.

That ominous run has reeled in Newcastle, Wimbledon, Arsenal and now Liverpool at the top of the league and restored the defending champions to the position they have made their own over the last four seasons.

But Saturday's clash at Old Trafford is as much about settling an old score as it is about racking up league points before United once again turn their attentions to the European Champions' League in early March.

When Alex Ferguson's side went to Southampton in October they were smarting from a 5-0 thrashing at Newcastle the previous weekend. Relegation-threatened Southampton were expected to feel the full brunt of an indignant United backlash.
But Graeme Souness's Saints pulled off an audacious 6-3 win which suggested the Newcastle result was not just a one-off glitch in United's season.

A sense of unease set in at Old Trafford and in the month that followed, they lost at home to Turkey's Fenerbahce, Chelsea and European champions Juventus before finally re-floating their fast-sinking ship in December.
A rejuvenated Andy Cole, who scored the late winner against Wimbledon, could form a new attacking partnership with Norway's Ole Gunnar Solksjaer, United's man-of-the-match in midweek.
United's squad is unchanged. Midfielder Nicky Butt is still out of action as he recovers from a badly bruised foot and defender Ronny Johnsen is close to a comeback but not close enough.

Southampton, dumped out of the League Cup by second division Stockport in midweek, will be without suspended midfielder Robbie Slater and Souness is likely to recall central defender Richard Dryden to shore up his leaky defence.

In London, Tottenham entertain Chelsea in a match which should be a happier affair than their previous meeting in October, played just four days after the death in a helicopter clash of Chelsea's high-profile benefactor Matthew Harding.
Spurs are still ridden by injuries and manager Gerry Francis says he is thoroughly fed up with having only half a squad to choose from.
Chelsea won that emotionally-charged match 3-1 and are on a roll after their thrilling 4-2 F.A. Cup victory over Liverpool last weekend.
